issues.t: Head or intake gasket failure and overheating
issues.sym: Coolant keeps dropping, the engine overheats at low speed or idle, white sweet-smelling smoke from the tailpipe, or milky oil. Sludge may show in the coolant reservoir.
issues.why: The 3.4L V6 is known for gasket failures that let coolant leak outside or into the engine. Many owners replaced thermostats and water pumps first before a head gasket was found to be the cause.
issues.next: If the gauge climbs, pull over and shut the engine off; driving hot can warp the heads. Have a cooling system pressure test and a combustion gas test before replacing parts.

issues.t: Heater blows only cold air
issues.sym: Air comes out of the vents but stays cold on the heat setting, and the defroster won't warm the windshield.
issues.why: The temperature blend door inside the dash breaks or sticks. The same flaw affects the Chevrolet Equinox. Reaching it can mean removing part of the dashboard.
issues.next: Check the coolant level first. If the windshield won't defrost, don't drive in cold or wet weather until it is fixed. Have a shop look at the blend door; most of the work is in reaching it.

issues.t: Under-hood fuse block can melt
issues.sym: A burning rubber smell while driving, then the engine stops. The fuse box and nearby wiring are found melted.
issues.why: Owners report the main fuse block under the hood overheating at high mileage. The exact cause hasn't been confirmed.
issues.next: If you smell burning plastic or rubber, pull over, shut the engine off and get out. Have the fuse box and wiring inspected before driving again.

issues.t: Cooling fan stops from melted connectors
issues.sym: The temperature climbs in traffic or at idle but is fine on the highway, because the radiator fan isn't running.
issues.why: The electrical connectors for the cooling fan overheat and melt.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Watch the temperature gauge in traffic. Have the fan circuit and connectors checked before it overheats the engine.

issues.t: Spark plug wires fail and cause misfires
issues.sym: The engine runs rough or shakes, the check engine light comes on or flashes, and it may keep coming back after a repair.
issues.why: Spark plug wire boots fail and plugs get carbon tracking, which lets the spark leak away. Owners say GM sent letters about it and some dealers extended coverage.
issues.next: A flashing check engine light means stop driving hard; it can damage the catalytic converter. Ask a dealer about extended coverage, and replace all the wires and plugs together.

issues.t: Timing chain wear on the 3.6L V6
issues.sym: Rattle at start-up, a check engine light with cam timing codes, or rough running.
issues.why: The timing chains on the 3.6L V6 can stretch. An owner reported a timing chain repair at about 56,000 miles.
issues.next: Have timing codes and noises checked early, before a chain jumps. Change the oil on time with the right oil.

issues.t: Power steering cuts out
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes heavy, sometimes with a StabiliTrak message, and may come back on its own later.
issues.why: The electric power steering system can lose assist. Owners report it across model years; one dealer quoted a full steering unit replacement.
issues.next: Steering still works but needs much more effort. Slow down, allow room, and have the power steering codes read. Check nhtsa.gov/recalls with your VIN.

issues.t: StabiliTrak and traction control lights come on
issues.sym: Service StabiliTrak and traction control lights, often with the check engine light. They may go away after the car sits, then return.
issues.why: Stability control complaints are the largest brake category for the 2007 Torrent at NHTSA. Causes include wheel speed sensors, communication faults and engine faults that switch the system off.
issues.next: The brakes still work, but stability control may be off, so drive gently on wet or icy roads. Have all modules scanned, not just the engine.

issues.t: ABS activates at low speed from a bad wheel sensor
issues.sym: The brake pedal pulses and grinds at slow speeds when stopping normally, or the ABS light is on.
issues.why: A failing wheel speed sensor, often at the rear, sends a false signal that a wheel is locking.
issues.next: Allow extra stopping distance. Have the ABS codes read to find which sensor is bad.

issues.t: Battery dies early or drains
issues.sym: The car won't start after sitting, needs frequent jump starts, or goes through batteries quickly.
issues.why: Owners report short battery life and drains. A damaged door wiring harness has been found causing drain on some.
issues.next: Have the battery and alternator tested. If the battery is good, ask for a parasitic draw test.

issues.t: Door wiring breaks and windows or locks stop working
issues.sym: Power window, lock, speaker or mirror on one door stops working, often all at once.
issues.why: Wires in the rubber boot between the door and the body break or get pinched from years of opening and closing.
issues.next: Have the harness in the door hinge area inspected. Repairing the broken wires is often an option instead of replacing parts.

issues.t: Alternator failure
issues.sym: Battery light on, dim lights, or the car dies while driving.
issues.why: Owners report alternator replacements between about 60,000 and 92,000 miles.
issues.next: If the battery light comes on, head somewhere safe soon; the car will run only until the battery is drained.

issues.t: AWD driveshaft center bearing or U-joint wear
issues.sym: A clunk when starting off, a vibration that grows with speed, or a squeak from under the middle of the vehicle on all-wheel-drive models.
issues.why: The rear driveshaft's center support (hanger) bearing and U-joints wear out.
issues.next: Have the driveshaft inspected soon. A failed bearing or joint can damage the driveshaft.

issues.t: AWD warning light in cold weather
issues.sym: The all-wheel-drive warning light comes on in cold weather.
issues.why: Owners report the AWD system flagging a fault in the cold, with no confirmed cause.
issues.next: Have the AWD codes read. Until fixed, assume the vehicle may be in front-wheel drive only on slippery roads.

issues.t: Transmission cooler lines leak
issues.sym: Red fluid drips under the front of the vehicle, or the transmission slips when low.
issues.why: The lines that carry transmission fluid to the radiator cooler leak, sometimes at low mileage.
issues.next: Check for red fluid under the front. Low fluid can ruin the transmission, so get the lines replaced soon.

issues.t: Wheel bearing and hub failure
issues.sym: A hum or growl that rises with speed, sometimes with the ABS light.
issues.why: Owners report replacing wheel hub bearing assemblies, sometimes more than one within months.
issues.next: Have it diagnosed soon. Bad hubs can also cause ABS faults.

issues.t: Front lower control arm rattle
issues.sym: Rattle or clunk from the front end over bumps.
issues.why: The front lower control arm bushings or ball joints wear.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. A worn ball joint should be replaced promptly.

issues.t: Check engine light from gas cap or EVAP leak
issues.sym: Check engine light, often after filling up.
issues.why: A loose or worn gas cap is the most reported Torrent problem. Faulty EVAP sensors and EGR valves also set the light at higher mileage.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks. If the light stays on, have the codes read.

issues.t: Fuel smell or leak at the tank
issues.sym: A fuel smell, gas leaking when you fill up, or a fuel gauge that stops working.
issues.why: Owners report leaks at the fuel tank. A GM bulletin mentions the plastic ports on the fuel pump module cracking.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't drive and don't park in a closed garage. Have the tank and pump module inspected.

issues.t: Corroded fuel lines leak
issues.sym: A gas smell or wet fuel lines under the vehicle.
issues.why: Steel fuel lines rust through with age and road salt.
issues.next: Don't drive with a fuel leak. Have the corroded lines replaced.

issues.t: Water collects in the spare tire well
issues.sym: Standing water under the rear cargo floor or in the wheel well, with a musty smell.
issues.why: Owners report water pooling under the cargo floor. It usually comes from a leaking rear seal or body plug, and it has no way to drain out.
issues.next: Dry it out to prevent rust and mold, then have the rear seals water-tested.

issues.t: Side moldings peel off
issues.sym: The body side moldings come loose or peel away.
issues.why: The adhesive on the side trim fails with age.
issues.next: Cosmetic only. Reattach or replace the molding before it falls off on the road.

issues.t: Airbag light from passenger seat sensor
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on, which can fail a safety inspection.
issues.why: The sensor that detects a front passenger fails.
issues.next: With the airbag light on, the airbags may not work. Have the system scanned and repaired.

issues.t: Roof rail airbags may not protect fully (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: The side curtain airbags didn't fully meet the federal head-protection standard. Covered by recall 07V-520.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Windshield may not stay attached in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: Some windshields were not bonded well enough to meet the federal standard. Covered by recall 07V-242.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. If the windshield has since been replaced, make sure a qualified glass shop did it.

issues.t: Passenger airbag status may be wrong (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag on/off light doesn't match who is in the seat.
issues.why: The passenger seat sensor was calibrated wrong on some vehicles. Covered by recall 07V-344.
issues.next: If the light looks wrong, move the passenger to the back seat. Check your VIN for the free fix.

issues.t: Squeaky serpentine belt
issues.sym: A squeak or chirp from the front of the engine.
issues.why: The serpentine belt wears or glazes, even at low mileage.
issues.next: Have the belt and tensioner checked. If the belt breaks, the alternator stops charging and the engine can overheat.
